description.narrative:
O BE UPDATED BY OIV
PROPOSED ACTIVITIES FOR IP 3 IN VIETNAM
1. Project partners: • Dragon Institute, Can Tho University: responsible for Mekong delta provinces and National level • CSRD: Responsible for Thua Thien Hue province and contributingto national advocacy. • WARECODE: Collaborator for water governance research and GEDSI at national level
2. Project location: Mekong Delta River provinces and Thua Thien Hue province (Srekong river basin) 3. Proposed project activities: During 2015–2024, the Mekong Inclusion Project have been working with thousands of women, ethnic minorities, vulnerable communities through coordinated by civil society organizations, universities, research institutions, private sector in Lao PDR, Cambodia, Myanmar,Vietnam and Thailand to ensure their rights accessed to essential river resources for their livelihoods, health, gender equality, disability and social inclusion and well-being. This concept note continues developing the ideas to scale up these achievements, narrow down challenges that faced during implementing IP2 of the Inclusion Project and provide more solutions for upcoming phase on climate change resilience in the Mekong delta and one part of Srekong river in Vietnam. Based on recommendations fromend of evaluation IP 2 report and discussion with main partners (CSRD and DRAGON) in Vietnam, there are several groups of activities proposed for each component to implement in Vietnam in next phase 3 which listed as below: 3.1. Water Resources Governance pilar
• Research on the impact of sediment reduction in Mekong riveron the agriculture production and fisheries of Mekong delta of Vietnam, and to recommend feasible solution, including natural basedsolutions for adaptation. • Research on the role and needs of private sector and CSOs participating in the water resource conservation by contributing to restore freshwater ecosystems, reforestation. The findings from research will (i) provide policy recommendations to the government for further providing instructions and guideline for CSOs, private sector’ roles, rights, responsibility and benefits in the Law on water resources ( revised in 2023) when contributing to restore freshwater ecosystems, reforestation in Vietnam and mechanism for CSOs playcoordinating roles between private sector and government in water resources conservation ; (ii) Building a network for private sector and CSOs on water resource conservation and reforestation • Research on biodiversity of fishery in the Srekong basin(apart of river belong to 3S rivers) for conserving endangered existence fish species and potential of raising aquaculture based on natural solutions to enhancing livelihood income for community people and promote fishery co-management among communities. •Join work with regional program
3.2. GEDSI pilar • Review and simplify GEDSI Impact Assessment tool. Design the guidelines and supporting CSOs, private sector and local government agencies to use in water resources conservation, reforestation andtoadopt CSR practices. • Capacity building for relevant stakeholders GEDSI and to integrate GEDSI into project activities and other relevant plans, especially the provincial master plan that this project will advocate for changes. • Documentation and dissemination of success stories on GEDSI tool application • Join work with regional program
3.3. Climate resilience pilar • Advocate for revision of MKD provincial agriculture master plan toward climate resilience and green development. Conduct comprehensiveassessment on (i) situation of climate change impact on agriculture and aquaculture in MKD provinces, (ii) the feasibility, cost-effectiveness, challenges and potential for development of current climate smart agriculture (CSA) models and other natural based solution for climate resilient models in the MKD. The research result will be used to advocate for revision of provincial master plan on agriculture and aquaculture development toward climate resilience and green development. • Research anddevelop amodel to expand mangrove forests into the mainland in the Mekong Delta. The purpose is to prepare in advance saving space of mangrove forests (free zone between sea water and mainland) to prevent landslides and erosion and to develop livelihoodmodelsunder the mangrove forests such as raising shrimp, clams, other aquatic products and honeybee farming. • Research and develop circular economy models for rice sector (rice straw and husk management) and aquaculture (e.g. catfish farming waste management) forrenewable energy, creating renew jobs for women and protect the environment and water conservation in the Mekong delta. • Research and develop climate resilience models for sustainable livelihood in MKD such as shrimp and rice or fish andrice rotation models, raising shrimp in mangrove forest, etc. • Develop the model of reforestation/forest improvement (planting multilayer forest structure) in upstream Srekong river areas to avoid land erosion, land slide, save soil nutrient and protect biodiversity of range forest in Truong Son Mountain. This model can improve poor forest and increase bio-diversity in the corridors between Lao PDR and Vietnam border and especially create alternative livelihood for ethnic minoritycommunities through planting herbs and non-timber products under the forest shadow for income generation and establish the community based on forest management • Promote the use of climate information system into community risk management plan and community agriculture development plan

Today, Oxfam works in 26 provinces with people, governments and civil society to promote equality and well-being through social and economic change.
